clue.text: Banger at first needs space to stop — it has a dreadful woman driver

definitions.text: it has a dreadful woman driver

indicators.note: at first means take only the opening letter

parts.note: room means space
to stick is to stop or get stuck

explanation.surface: An old car needs space to brake because a terrible female motorist is at the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for an old car, which makes 'driver' look like motoring; the dreadful woman is a witch, riding a broom.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch, a fearsome woman in folklore, rides and steers this through the sky.

clue.text: Sound to write down for composer

indicators.note: sound tells you to say a word for writing down and hear what it sounds like

parts.note: to list is to write items down

explanation.surface: Someone told to note the sound looks for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz LISZT, the Hungarian pianist-composer, is pronounced like LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a celebrated nineteenth-century Hungarian composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: A rat starting to epitomise my school

parts.note: a cad, like a rat, is a dishonourable man

indicators.note: starting means take the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A scoundrel is starting to embody the spirit of someone's school.
explanation.definitionFit: An academy is a place of learning, particularly a specialised or secondary institution.

clue.text: Something to go on red flower — blue

parts.note: lava is red-hot rock that flows, so a 'flower' in the sense of something that flows
blue is the colour of Britain's Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a red bloom with a touch of blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is not a bloom but a thing that flows: molten lava. TORY is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, whose colour is blue.
explanation.definitionFit: A toilet is, euphemistically, somewhere you go, and 'go on' is a jokey description of using it.

clue.text: Storyteller made front of audience sit up

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: A storyteller made the people in front of the audience sit up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses POSE to ESOP, since in a down clue up reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek author of the famous fables.

clue.text: Hotel in gold overlooking Norwegian port, unfinished

indicators.note: overlooking in a down clue puts the gold above the port

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Bergen is a major port on Norway's west coast

explanation.surface: A golden hotel overlooks a Norwegian harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' cuts the final N off BERGEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An auberge is a French inn, a place offering lodging to travellers.

clue.text: Insects full of energy, one holds, in part of Tertiary

indicators.note: holds means the word one wraps around the rest

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: full of puts the word for energy inside the insects

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Energetic insects are trapped in a lump of Tertiary rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of' puts the energy word inside the insects, and 'holds' wraps one around that. The Tertiary is the old name for the geological period after the Cretaceous.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oligocene is an epoch of the Tertiary geological period, roughly 34 to 23 million years ago.

clue.text: Pull one over the pond

definitions.meaning: an American, someone across the Atlantic from Britain

explanation.definitionFit: A sharp tug is a yank, and Britons call an American a Yank.

clue.text: In secret,'e's having an intimate relationship

indicators.note: in places the word with a dropped H inside the word for secret

parts.note: closet as an adjective means secret or hidden
the dropped-aitch form of he's leaves E plus S

explanation.surface: Someone says in Cockney that he is secretly in a close relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: ''e's' is 'he's' with the H dropped, as in Cockney speech, leaving ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Things close-set are positioned near together, a closely related arrangement.

clue.text: These block castle, so bishop moves

indicators.note: moves suggests the pieces shifting around the board, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A chess player's castle is blocked as a bishop shifts across the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' turns CASTLESOB, the letters of castle, so and B, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstacles are barriers or hindrances, things that block the way forward.

clue.text: Child leads in babies, all in red nappies

indicators.note: leads are the front letters, so take the initial of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Every baby in a nursery is wearing a red nappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scottish and northern English word for a youngster or offspring.

clue.text: She has the right, above all, to follow order around

indicators.note: around tells you to turn the letters for order back to front

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
taken as written
superior means higher than all others, above all

explanation.surface: Someone claims an overriding right to boss people about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the Order of Merit's letters back to front, and 'to follow' sets the rest after them. 'order' hints at a religious order, which fits the head of a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a convent is a woman, so the pronoun stands in for this female religious leader.

clue.text: Terribly sacred holy books, a line appearing priestly

indicators.note: terribly means the word sacred is badly mangled and rearranged

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Sacred texts and a line of verse sound appropriately clerical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges SACRED to SACERD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacerdotal relates to priests and the priesthood.

clue.text: Drink rum in outskirts of Torquay

indicators.note: in places the word for rum inside the letters on the edges of the town name
outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of the following word

parts.note: rum in British slang means strange, odd

explanation.surface: Someone orders a rum on the edge of an English seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but means odd. Torquay is a seaside resort in Devon; its first and last letters are T and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot alcoholic drink of spirits with water, sugar and spices.

clue.text: Spade is one device — test out without spades

indicators.note: out signals the letters of device and test are jumbled, and without removes the spades letter from that pool

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A gadget for testing is used without spades.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Spade is the private eye in Dashiell Hammett's The Maltese Falcon. 'out' scrambles DEVICETEST, and 'without' removes the S for spades first.
explanation.definitionFit: Sam Spade is a fictional private investigator, so he is an example.

clue.text: Small groups want information on boat times

indicators.note: on places the information after the boat

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a kind of boat
gen is British slang for information
an era is a period of time, a span of times

explanation.surface: Someone needs details of a boat's timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal slang for information or facts.
explanation.definitionFit: In biological classification a subgenus is a smaller division within a genus.

clue.text: Composer pinching a number of Mozart's, and shot from behind

indicators.note: pinching means holding, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach is the composer
Mozart's works are numbered in the Kochel catalogue, abbreviated K
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer steals one of Mozart's pieces and fires from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Mozart's works are catalogued by Köchel numbers, written K.
explanation.definitionFit: A backhand is a tennis stroke played with the back of the hand facing forward.

clue.text: Releasing deer with lion stalking, one heading for confrontation

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
a hart is a male deer
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A lion stalks a deer, heading for a showdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stalking' places the lion in front of the deer it follows. A HART is an adult male red deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathartic experience provides emotional release, purging pent-up feelings.

clue.text: An individual passing empty day, lacking inspiration

indicators.note: passing means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: empty removes the inside, leaving first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone spends an empty day without inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips the middle of day, and 'passing' wraps the individual around what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means bland and inoffensive, so dull and uninspired.

clue.text: Tantrum, bit of an act

definitions.meaning: making a ... means throwing an angry public outburst
a play's act is divided into smaller sections

explanation.definitionFit: A scene is both an emotional outburst in public and a subdivision of a theatrical act.

clue.text: Work on story with plot breaking hearts, perhaps

indicators.note: breaking means splitting one word to fit another inside

parts.note: hearts is one example of a card suit
a bed is a garden plot

explanation.surface: A story is about a plot that breaks hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is a garden plot, a BED, not a storyline; 'perhaps' marks hearts as one example of a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to prepare a news article for publication.

clue.text: Where draughts go, in any case

definitions.meaning: draughts, the British name for checkers, move over the playing surface
applying to all equally, in every instance

explanation.definitionFit: Draughts pieces travel over a checkerboard; the idiom also means applying universally to everyone.

clue.text: In auction, black is black

indicators.note: in puts the letter for black inside the word for auction

parts.note: a sale is an auction
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: In an auction, a black lot is declared black.
explanation.walkthrough: SABLE is the heraldic term for black.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic name for the colour black.

clue.text: Muslim commander popular — Muslim commander popular!

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander or chief
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A Muslim commander's popularity is repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the same thing twice: the repeat of the phrase is the definition, meaning once more.
explanation.definitionFit: The repeated phrase says the thing a second time, which is what the word for once more means.

clue.text: Communication by flier

definitions.meaning: a talk or conversation between people
the stonechat and whinchat are small birds

explanation.definitionFit: Informal talk is a form of communication, and the bird known as a stonechat flies.

clue.text: Armpits can be alarming

definitions.meaning: armpits often grow plenty of underarm growth
informal British slang for frightening or dangerous

explanation.definitionFit: Underarms can be covered in growth, and a frightening experience is informally described the same way.

clue.text: Margin absurd, investing Rockefeller's capital payment

parts.note: a bank is the edge or margin of a river

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so one word's letters wrap the other

parts.note: daft means foolish or absurd

indicators.note: a word's capital is its first letter

explanation.surface: Absurd margins are being invested with Rockefeller money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investing' and 'capital' suggest finance, fitting Rockefeller, but they put the R of Rockefeller inside DAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank draft is a cheque drawn by a bank on itself, a guaranteed form of payment.

clue.text: Support doubled round first of ropes — daughter seemed likely to fall

indicators.note: round puts the doubled support around the first letter of ropes
doubled means the word for support appears twice in a row

parts.note: a tee is a peg supporting a golf ball

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter

explanation.surface: A climber's support, doubled round the ropes, wobbles as a daughter nearly falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled' gives TEETEE, and 'round' wraps it around R so the R sits in the second TEE. A golf TEE supports the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to wobble unsteadily, on the verge of toppling over.

clue.text: Without a key, some of villa not accessible from the back

indicators.note: from the back means read the letters from right to left
some of the words means a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Part of a villa cannot be reached from the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of' takes LANOTA from vilLA NOT Accessible, and 'from the back' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonal music is written without a tonal centre, so it has no key.
